key_insight: PYTHIA combines a frozen pretrained model, transformer-based adaptation, and Gaussian processes to guide defect and adsorption-site optimization with limited target data.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce data requirements when searching for favorable defects and adsorption sites in understudied materials.
method: Pretrain a foundation model on chemically similar molecules using a physically related prediction target.
Freeze pretrained weights and train a transformer layer for subspace alignment plus Gaussian processes for uncertainty quantification.
Use the adapted model as a surrogate for Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports applications to adsorption and defect optimization in two distinct systems, but the provided text is truncated and contains no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Transfer effectiveness should be validated when target materials differ substantially from the chemically similar pretraining data.
paper_title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
